**Structure of Bacteria:**
Bacteria are single-celled prokaryotic microorganisms lacking a true membrane-bound nucleus and membrane-bound organelles. 
- **Cell Envelope:** Consists of an outer capsule (protection), cell wall (rigidity, composed of peptidoglycan), and plasma membrane (selective permeability).
- **Cytoplasm:** Contains 70S ribosomes, inclusion bodies, and a single circular chromosome located in an irregular region called the **nucleoid**.
- **Appendages:** Flagella (for motility), pili/fimbriae (for adhesion and conjugation).

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[Bacterial Cell] --> B[Cell Envelope]
    A --> C[Cytoplasm & Nucleoid]
    A --> D[Surface Appendages]
    B --> B1[Capsule]
    B --> B2[Cell Wall]
    B --> B3[Plasma Membrane]
    C --> C1[70S Ribosomes]
    C --> C2[Nucleoid DNA]
    D --> D1[Flagella]
    D --> D2[Pili/Fimbriae]
    style A fill:#f9f,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
```

**Shape, Size, and Morphology:**
- **Size:** Typically ranges from $0.5\ \mu\text{m}$ to $5.0\ \mu\text{m}$ in length.
- **Shape & Morphology:**
  1. *Coccus (Spherical):* e.g., *Staphylococcus*
  2. *Bacillus (Rod-shaped):* e.g., *Escherichia coli*
  3. *Spirillum (Spiral/Corkscrew):* e.g., *Spirillum volutans*
  4. *Vibrio (Comma-shaped):* e.g., *Vibrio cholerae*
proTip: Always mention the absence of a true nucleus and presence of 70S ribosomes to highlight the prokaryotic nature of bacteria.
